## Introduction

This site provides supplementary information to help enable reproduction and independent exploration of the statistical analyses reported in Cooper _et al._ (2026).

The pages in the `Analyses` section describe regression modelling for the manuscript "Structural and functional basis of lipid-associated, electrogenic ammonium transport by the Rhesus-family protein NeRh50 in _Nitrosomonas europaea_" by Cooper _et al._ We analyse this data to establish evidence in support of answers to the following key questions:

1. Do maximum amplitude and/or decay rate constant vary for WT NeRh50 in response to changes in lipid-protein ratio (LPR)?
2. Do maximum amplitude and/or decay rate constant vary for WT NeRh50 in response to a change in substrate from NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> to MeA?
3. Do maximum amplitude and/or decay rate constant vary for WT NeRh50 in response to a changes in pH conditions?

## Datasets

The underlying data for these analyses can be downloaded from the links below

- [fig_4c.csv](assets/data/fig_4c.csv)
- [fig_5a.csv](assets/data/fig_5a.csv)
- [fig_5b.csv](assets/data/fig_5b.csv)
- [fig_6b.csv](assets/data/fig_6b.csv)
- [fig_6d.csv](assets/data/fig_6d.csv)

The datasets are presented in @tbl-load-data.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-load-data
#| tbl-cap: "Data for Cooper _et al._ _Data for maximum amplitude and decay rate constant at three LPR values, for WT Rh50._"
#| tbl-subcap:
#|    - "Maximum amplitude and decay rate constant at three LPR values, for WT Rh50 (figure 4c)."
#|    - "Maximum amplitude and decay rate constant k for NH₄⁺ and MeA (figure 5a)."
#|    - "Maximum amplitude and decay rate constant k for transient current measured after a 200 mM ammonium pulse in proteoliposomes containing NeRh50 at LPR10, at four pH conditions (figure 6b)."
#|    - "Maximum amplitude and decay rate constant for representative SSME transient currents recorded at pH5-pH8 (figure 6d)."
#|    - "Maximum amplitude and decay rate constant for transient currents recorded in the presence of 200 mM NH₄⁺ under static pH (pH6.5), in the presence of an inward proton gradient (pH6.5 to 7.5), and in the absence of NH4+ under the same proton-gradient configuration (figure 6f)."
#| layout-ncol: 1

# Use helper script to load dataframes
source("assets/r/load_dataframes.R")
dfms <- load_dataframes()

# Show interactive tables of data
DT::datatable(dfms$dfm_4c, options=list(pageLength=5))
DT::datatable(dfms$dfm_5a, options=list(pageLength=5))
DT::datatable(dfms$dfm_6b, options=list(pageLength=5))
DT::datatable(dfms$dfm_6d, options=list(pageLength=5))
DT::datatable(dfms$dfm_6f, options=list(pageLength=5))
```
